evals.prompt: Define frontend architecture in 2-3 sentences. Name the three decisions it governs and what distinguishes the architecture from the folder tree.
expected_elements: Names the three decisions: where code lives (module/folder structure), what may depend on what (import direction), who owns mutable state
States the import graph — not the folder tree — is the real architecture
Mentions the three component layers (primitives, composed, connected) and/or server-vs-client state as covered concerns
Frames it as making placement/dependency/ownership decisions reproducible and enforceable

evals.prompt: Why is a tidy, deeply-categorized folder tree NOT evidence of good frontend architecture? What is the load-bearing structure instead?
expected_elements: The import graph, not the folder names, determines what can change independently
A pretty tree with cyclic feature imports is worse than a flat folder with strict one-way dependencies
Optimize for cohesion (what changes together stays together) and colocation (where would I look for this)
Direction must be enforced (boundary linter) or it degrades within months

evals.prompt: A team mixes server-fetched data and ephemeral UI state in a single global store. What problem does this cause and how should the two be separated?
expected_elements: Mixing them produces cache-invalidation bugs that look like rendering bugs
Server state (remote, cache-managed) and client state (UI-only, ephemeral) are different problems with different requirements
Use one fetch/cache/revalidate tool for server data
Reserve global client state for genuinely cross-cutting UI concerns (theme, current user, route)

evals.prompt: Describe the three component layers and identify which boundary most often produces dependency tangles, and why.
expected_elements: Primitives (no business knowledge, props-only — Button, Input, Stack)
Composed components (combine primitives with feature layout, no data fetching — OrderSummary, AddressForm)
Connected components (own fetching, mutation, routing — OrderDetailPage)
The composed↔connected boundary is the most common tangle source: a 'shared' composed component reaching into a feature store creates a back-edge

evals.prompt: What four axes do state-shape decisions span, and what does the shape choice determine?
expected_elements: Location (component, context, store)
Normalization (entity-keyed vs nested)
Derivation (computed at read time vs stored)
Ownership (who can write)
The shape determines what re-renders, what stays consistent across views, and where mutation-misses become bugs

evals.prompt: A teammate asks the frontend-architecture skill to pick the brand color palette and decide whether to use CSS-in-JS or Tailwind. Is that in scope? Why or why not?
expected_elements: Color palette is out of scope — that is visual design (color-system-design / visual-design-foundations)
CSS-in-JS vs Tailwind is a styling/framework-tactic choice, not structural — this skill is framework-neutral
Correctly distinguishes structure/dependency/ownership (in scope) from visual and framework-tactic decisions (out of scope)

evals.prompt: A lead says 'we have a clean, well-organized folder structure, so our architecture is solid.' Correct the mental model.
expected_elements: Folder structure is not the architecture; the import graph is
A clean tree can still have cyclic feature imports and back-edges — architecturally worse than a flat tree with one-way deps
Real soundness requires enforced import direction (boundary linter at PR time) and cohesion, not categorization
A 'shared' component reaching into a feature store is a violation regardless of how tidy the folders look

evals.prompt: What concrete, checkable signals would you inspect to verify a frontend's architecture is sound?
expected_elements: An import-boundary linter is configured and CI fails the build on violations
Any feature folder can be removed without touching code outside it except a single registration point
A new dev can name where any code lives in ~30 seconds given feature name + kind (UI/data/logic)
Server state is fetched through one mechanism (fetch call sites ≈ distinct endpoints, not multiples)
No feature-specific names in shared/ primitives; re-render counts can be measured and explained
